identity.mechanic: **The court decides when things happen in a fight.** Its units strike before their turn, arrive halfway through, knock enemies out of their turn, or hold everything back and let it go at once. Two new keywords:

keywords.name: Gust
keywords.text: this unit attacks right now, out of turn. It's a normal attack in every way (random front-row enemy, takes damage back), and the unit still makes its usual attack in the cycle. A Gust that happens twice or more is still one Gust for cards that count Gusts; each of its attacks gets that Gust's effects.

keywords.name: Late
keywords.text: if this is in your hand when the fight starts, it waits, then arrives after your side's third attack (Gusts count), in your first empty slot in reading order, or as soon as a slot opens. If your board empties first, it arrives at once instead and the fight goes on. Late units arriving together land in hand order, left to right. It didn't start the fight, so it doesn't count for who attacks first or for hero damage. After the fight it's back in your hand. Played to the board, it's an ordinary unit.

keywords.name: knocked flat
keywords.text: the unit skips its next attack.

identity.plays: Early, Gust Pages and Sir Vane win fights by hitting before the enemy can. Then the hand becomes a second board. A Late unit is an eighth (or ninth) unit that the enemy's Start of Combat can't touch, and it lands mid-fight onto whatever the enemy has left. Most of the court's growth comes from counting how often it Gusted, so every Gust source also feeds growth somewhere else. The puzzle is ordering: who you played last (Vane), who stands next to the empty slot (The Helm), how many attacks happen before the Duke arrives, and when Lady High Pressure should die. Many cards do a second job: Mr Fair's exit dodges a death, Black Cloud's speed-up shrinks the Duke's count, and the Wild Hunt makes the dead count as arrivals.

units.name: Gust Page
units.text: Start of Combat: Gust. If another Gust Page Gusted before this, it first gains +2 Attack (it sulks).

units.name: Windhover
units.text: Faces into the wind: the first time each other friendly unit Gusts in a fight, this permanently gains +1/+1. Twice a fight.

units.name: Sir Vane, the Weathercock
units.text: Points at the last other unit you played (his pointer shows on the board and stays until you play another). If that unit is sold or leaves your board, he points at nothing. Start of Combat: that unit Gusts. Whenever a friendly unit arrives Late, it Gusts too; his pointer doesn't move.

units.name: The Swift Couriers
units.text: Late. Never lands while recruiting: can't be played from your hand (you can sell it). When it arrives, it takes its slot and fights, and your unit nearest that slot Gusts.

units.name: Keeper of the Glass
units.text: Start of Turn: read the glass. If your units Gusted or arrived Late 3+ times last fight (Change), gain 1 gold; 6+ times (Stormy), gain 2 instead.

units.name: The Helm
units.text: Won't budge: can't be moved once played. Mentions his name to everyone: when you play a unit next to him, it permanently gains +1/+1 for each turn he has stood there (up to +4/+4). A unit that arrives Late next to him gains the same for the fight.

units.name: Old Föhn
units.text: Warm: whenever another friendly unit Gusts, it permanently gains +1/+1. Three times a fight. Blamed for everything: whenever a friendly unit dies, Föhn gains +2 Attack.

units.name: Beacon-Keeper of the Ridgeway
units.text: Start of Combat: light the beacons. The next two units after this along the touching chain Gust, in order. A gap puts the beacons out.

units.name: Mr Fair
units.text: When played, add Mrs Foul to your hand. End of Turn: the units beside him permanently gain +1/+1. Never home together: when Mrs Foul arrives, he goes indoors (leaves the fight; not a death) and she takes his slot.

units.name: Countess Bora
units.text: Her attacks knock their target flat. Late. When she arrives, she Gusts.
units.golden: 10/8. Target skips its next two attacks; Gusts twice.

units.name: Lord Mistral, Warden of the Rhône
units.text: Clears the room: your first three Gusts each fight also hit the enemies beside their target.

units.name: Dew-Pond Heron
units.text: Start of Turn: the leftmost Late unit in your hand permanently gains +1/+1 for each Gust and Late arrival your side made last fight (up to +8/+8). With none in hand, your biggest unit on the board gains it.

units.name: Black Cloud, Usher of the Court
units.text: Your Late units arrive after your second attack instead of your third. Announces every arrival: whenever a friendly unit arrives Late, it permanently gains +2/+2.

units.name: Duke Cumulonimbus, the Thunderhead
units.text: Late. Arrives late and loud: when he arrives, he counts the gap, gaining +2/+2 for each attack made so far this fight by either side (Gusts count). Then he Gusts.

units.name: Steward of the Bag of Winds
units.text: Your units' Gusts happen twice. Each is still one Gust for cards that count Gusts.

units.name: The Sí Gaoithe
units.text: A whirlwind on a still day. Start of Combat: lift the biggest enemy out of the fight. It drops back knocked flat into its slot (or the nearest empty one) after your third attack, or at once if every other enemy has died.

units.name: Her Serene Stillness, Lady High Pressure
units.text: Forbids anything to happen: while she lives, your Gusts wait, and so do Late units once their time to arrive has come. The Storm breaks when she dies, when she's your last unit, or after your sixth attack (waiting Gusts don't count until they happen): each waiting Gust whose unit still lives happens twice, in the order they waited, then every waiting Late unit arrives. Late units not yet due arrive at their usual time. After the Storm, nothing waits.
units.golden: 6/24. Each waiting Gust happens three times.

units.name: Master of the Wild Hunt
units.text: Late. Rides the winter storm: when he arrives, every friendly unit that has died this fight rides in with him, in reading order, back in its slot (or the nearest empty one) with 1 Health. They count as arriving Late, and each Gusts.

units.name: The Tower of the Winds
units.text: Eight faces. Start of Turn: each different unit of yours that Gusted last fight takes a face (up to 8). The units on your board permanently gain +1/+1 for each face taken.

extras.name: Mrs Foul
extras.text: (3/4, Created): Late. Can't be played from your hand while recruiting (you can sell it). When she arrives: if your Mr Fair is on the board, she takes his slot, he goes indoors, and she counts as having started the fight; otherwise she lands like any Late unit. Your other units gain +1 Attack. Golden 6/8, +2 Attack.

extras.name: "Nearest" ties
extras.text: "Nearest" ties go to the first slot in reading order. A Late unit that Gusts counts as yours for the Tower, the Glass and the Heron.

builds.name: Squall (Start of Combat Gusts)
builds.text: Gust Pages, Sir Vane, Beacon-Keeper, then Mistral and the Steward. You clear most of the front row before the enemy swings. Growth comes from counting Gusts: Windhover and Föhn early, the Heron at Tier 4 (on your biggest unit if you hold no Late units), the Tower at Tier 6. The Tower and Windhover reward *different* Gusters, so you spread Gusts across the board instead of doubling one unit. Example turn: Beacon-Keeper on F1 lights B1 and F2; Vane points at the Bora you just played (as a board unit), so her Gust knocks a big front-liner flat before it attacks.

builds.name: Late Entrance (the hand as a second board)
builds.text: Couriers, Mrs Foul, Bora, the Duke, the Wild Hunt, with Black Cloud and The Helm. You fight with up to seven on the board and two or three more in the wings. Leave a slot open next to The Helm in reading order so each arrival lands there and takes his buff. Vane makes every arrival Gust. Black Cloud's permanent +2/+2 grows the Late units in your hand each fight, and the Heron grows your leftmost one each turn. Arrivals land in hand order, so the leftmost card in hand takes The Helm's slot. The tension: Black Cloud brings arrivals in sooner, which shrinks the Duke's count. Johnny chooses which one wins.

builds.name: Calm Before the Storm
builds.text: Lady High Pressure, the Steward, the Duke and a Hunker or Shield neutral. Every Start of Combat Gust and every arrival is held while the enemy spends its own Start of Combat effects into her 12 Health. When she falls, the held Gusts happen twice each (four times with the Steward), then the Late units land at once, and the Duke counts a long gap. Put her in the front row for a fast storm, or in the back row to make it break on the sixth attack instead.

builds.name: Wild Hunt finish
builds.text: Let cheap units die early (Gust Pages trading into the front row), then the Master brings them all back as arrivals. Each one Gusts, takes Black Cloud's permanent +2/+2, and triggers Vane and The Helm again.

builds.name: Mixing in a lobby
builds.text:
- **Hunters:** Pack joins attacks by units beside it. A Gust is an attack, so a Pack unit beside a Gust Page joins its Start of Combat swing. Knocking a Quarry flat keeps your Hunter's target in place.
- **Fairies:** Late units land in your first empty slot. Put a Ring on that slot and every arrival gets the Ring size.
- **Bog folk:** Mire forces the enemy across to attack your Mire unit. That protects Lady High Pressure in the back, or forces hits onto Mr Fair just before he goes indoors.
- **Oozes:** an Ooze's Belly is the board-side twin of Late. Föhn's "blamed" Attack fires on every Ooze death.
- **Birds:** the Couriers are swifts. Selling Birds to Fly South leaves Nests, which are empty slots Late units can land in once the Egg dies.
- **Neutrals:** Swoop on a Gusting unit lets Start of Combat hits reach the back row. Shield keeps Gust Pages alive through the counter-damage.

risks: **Fights get hard to read.** Out-of-turn attacks, held Gusts and mid-fight arrivals pile up. This tribe needs the clearest combat animation: a visible queue, arrivals entering from the hand, a counter for the Duke.
**Gusts take damage back.** Early Gusts into big blockers or Bristle kill your own small units. That's intended friction, but the T1–2 experience may feel like suicide against Bog folk.
**The hand is crowded.** Late units compete with triples in progress, Acorn items and the 4-card limit. Hand-locked Couriers and Mrs Foul need selling from hand, which Bramble hasn't settled.
**Recorded boards must include the hand.** Asynchronous play has to store the hand and the Late rules.
**Late builds attack second.** Arrivals don't count for who goes first. Fine, but test whether Late is too weak against fast Start of Combat tribes.

**In-fight multipliers stack.** High Pressure ×2 with the Steward ×2 is ×4, and two goldens make it ×9. Every permanent gain is capped (once a fight, three times, up to 8 faces), so this is fight-only, but one-sided wipes could feel unfair to the loser.
**Thin economy.** The Glass is the only gold card, though it now pays for Late arrivals too. The tribe may lean on neutral gold support.

**Lady High Pressure can stall.** If your side never reaches six attacks, the Storm now breaks when she is your last unit, so it can no longer stay held to the end; watch whether the late break still feels bad.
**The Duke's count includes enemy attacks,** so he's strongest against wide boards. That could be swingy.
**The Wild Hunt plus Black Cloud** permanently buffs every revived unit. Bounded by deaths, but check it in practice.

tier_check.note: Page 2/2 at body 4, about 0.7 body in fight with a partner (target ~0.6). Windhover gives up to +4 stats a turn with two different Gusters, about 1 body (target 0.4), **over on purpose** as the Squall seed that rewards spreading Gusts.

Vane makes one Gust plus arrival Gusts, about 1 body in fight (target ~1). Glass pays about 1 gold. The Couriers are about 1.5 bodies in fight (an extra body plus a Gust), **over on purpose**: they cost a hand slot and arrive late.

Föhn up to 6 permanent stats a turn (0.86 body, target 0.8). The Helm about +8 once per play (target 1–1.4 bodies). Beacon makes two Gusts, about 1.3 bodies in fight. Mr Fair gives 4 permanent plus about 5 in fight across two cards. All within range.

Bora is about 2 bodies in fight (two enemy attacks skipped plus a Gust). The Heron averages about 10 stats a turn (1.2 bodies, target 1.3), now usually onto a Late unit in hand. Black Cloud is about 1 body permanent plus faster arrivals. Mistral is about 3 bodies in fight, **over on purpose** as the tribe's first multiplier, and capped at three Gusts.

The Duke typically gains +16 to +24 stats plus a Gust, about 4 bodies (target ~4). The Steward is about 3.3 bodies. The Sí Gaoithe's denial is hard to price, roughly 3–4 bodies of tempo, a little more now that its target drops back knocked flat. On guide.

The Tower with five faces gives about 70 permanent stats (5 bodies, target ~4, top ~10), slightly high as the Squall payoff. The Wild Hunt is about 5–6 bodies in fight. High Pressure is about 4 bodies alone, more with the Duke and the Steward, as the capstone multiplier.

rationale: **Gust Pages first** ("all want to go first"): a unit that attacks out of turn, so Gust came from them.
**Sir Vane** changes sides with every arrival, so he points at the last unit played. Play order becomes a decision.
**Duke Cumulonimbus** arrives late and counts lightning to thunder. A unit entering mid-fight that grows with the count became Late, played from the hand.
**Swifts never land:** a hand-only Late unit gave Late a cheap entry at Tier 2.
**The weather house, never home together:** a board-and-hand pair that swap mid-fight, so Late is more than an extra body.
**Seen together,** the cards all bent *when* things happen: first, last, skipped or held. That precedence became the identity, with Gust and Late as its two halves.
**Lady High Pressure forbids anything to happen:** holding both Gusts and arrivals, then releasing them doubled, ties the two keywords into one capstone.
**Bora and Mistral** took their real winds' effects (knocking people flat, clearing the room) so the Gust build has texture beyond more damage.
**Growth counts Gusts** (Windhover, Föhn, the Glass, the Heron, the Tower), each with a cap, so permanent growth stays priced while fight multipliers can run wild.
**The Wild Hunt** rides the storm and brings the dead back as arrivals, so every arrival trigger fires again. That's the Late capstone.
**The Sí Gaoithe** turns the court's timing on the enemy: the one card that delays their side.
**Economy stays one card,** because the hand-as-reserve already makes the tribe pay in hand space.

changes.what: Late: arrives at once if your board empties; several arrivals land in hand order. Gust: a repeated Gust counts once.
changes.why: An emptied board, arrival order and how repeats count for Gust counters were all unsaid.

changes.what: Grows the first time each other unit Gusts, twice a fight, instead of once a fight.
changes.why: Flattest seed; now it rewards spreading Gusts across units, like the Tower.

changes.what: If the pointed unit is sold or leaves the board, he points at nothing.
changes.why: What the pointer did after a sale or triple was unsaid.

changes.what: Grows your leftmost Late unit in hand; your biggest board unit only if you hold none.
changes.why: Generic target; now it grows the second board and adds a hold-or-play choice.

changes.what: Card now says each doubled Gust still counts as one Gust.
changes.why: Whether the repeat fed Gust counters was unsaid; counting once keeps the Glass and caps meaningful.

changes.what: The lifted enemy drops back knocked flat, and at once if every other enemy has died.
changes.why: Fight end with the enemy lifted was unsaid; knock-flat links it to Bora.

changes.what: Late units wait only once they're due; Storm also breaks when she's your last unit.
changes.why: Whether she brought the Duke in early was unsaid; she could also hold everything to a loss.

changes.what: The dead ride in, and Gust, in reading order.
changes.why: The order of a group arrival was unsaid.
